A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L2S research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MMSafetyBench, POPE, and COCO/CHAIR experiments, alongside qualitative examples, steering-vector analyses, and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Qwen2-VL evaluations, prompting comparisons, and selective-steering experiments on VLGuard.

M1.justification: The core P2S construction and L2S prediction procedure remain unchanged. For the new selective-steering variant, Appendix A.1 introduces zero steering targets for safe queries and explicitly replaces the auxiliary network's Tanh activation with ReLU. This is a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds VLGuard with safe and unsafe image-instruction queries and the distinct requirement of preserving default answers to safe queries. This substantially extends safety coverage from behavior-specific response correction to selective intervention. MMSafetyBench, POPE, and COCO captioning coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The Prompt baseline is newly evaluated in the MMSafetyBench and POPE comparisons in Tables 1–2. Existing comparators remain in their corresponding experiments. The VLGuard experiment uses existing No-steering and mean-steering comparators, with Mean-S and Mean-S(BA) identified as equivalent for that setup.

E3.justification: v2 extends the principal evaluations to Qwen2-VL-7B and adds VLGuard protocols measuring safe-answer preservation and preference against Mean-S, using steering and context layer 15. Appendix B.3.2 also changes POPE answer extraction from the first 20 generated tokens to the first 12. This is an explicit reported protocol revision, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.1 examines whether steering unnecessarily alters benign responses, using answer-preservation measurements and a paired safe/unsafe qualitative example. Existing failure cases, steering-vector geometry analyses, and steering-layer, magnitude, and context-layer ablations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Section 4.3 newly states that POPE Norm-Rnd results are averaged over four random seeds; v1 supplies no corresponding run count. This disclosure does not establish an increase in runs. The existing two-sided t-tests and p-values remain unchanged in v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 5.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces LLaVA POPE values, including L2S Random accuracy changing from 87.71% to 86.46%; the changed answer-parsing window prevents treating this as a clean same-setting performance decline. v2 adds Prompt and Qwen results and VLGuard outcomes, including 87.4% safe-answer preservation for L2S versus 5.2% for Mean-S. Existing LLaVA MMSafetyBench and CHAIR values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, the reconstruction formulation, and the CHAIR definitions are retained. v2 introduces no new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: input-dependent contrastive steering, a lightweight predictor of steering vectors, and improved safety and hallucination mitigation. The additional experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 discusses prompting's model-dependent safety benefits and weaker expert deference. Appendix A.1 adds an interpretation of selective steering as preserving useful benign responses while avoiding mean steering's unnecessary harmful-query framing. Section 5's limitations and the existing mechanism discussions remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies exact Prompt baseline instructions, Qwen completion examples, and settings for the VLGuard adaptation. The code link changes from mshukor/xl-vlms to jayneelparekh/learn-to-steer. Expanded main-text explanations of forced-answer completions largely clarify procedures already documented in v1 Appendix B.4; the combined losses, initialization, and token averaging were already disclosed.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Kingma and Welling's Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes and Shen et al.'s InterfaceGAN to connect steering with earlier latent-space image editing. The existing positioning against language-model and multimodal steering remains intact. Qwen2-VL and the work supplying VLGuard were already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory revisions, inserts the selective-steering subsection, adds acknowledgements, and updates the publication footer. Citations change from author-year to numbered format. Most existing prose and the overall section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain Prompt columns and separate Qwen panels; v2 adds the VLGuard table and qualitative figure and expands the completion-example boxes. Figure 2 is relocated, while existing figures and analyses are retained with renumbering. These are localized display extensions within the same overall visual design.

improvement.justification: Qwen2-VL evaluation tests generality beyond v1's single model, Prompt supplies a useful inexpensive comparator, and VLGuard directly tests preservation of benign responses. These strengthen the empirical assessment. However, Section 4.2 retains an all-behaviors superiority claim despite Mean-S(BA)'s better Qwen unsafe scores, and Table 2 shows Prompt outperforming L2S on LLaVA POPE Popular. The broader evidence improves the paper, but incomplete reconciliation of claims and results limits the net gain.
